# The calendar month view shows no days when there are no calendars

> Reserved for @sloemo01, who found this while writing #19006's component-tier witness. The maintainer team will not claim it.

## Context

A month view with no calendars shows its header and an empty scroll area: no weeks and no days. @sloemo01 measured it in the component tier on #19006: `weekCount: 0, dayCount: 0`. Their comments there trace the chain.

## The Problem

Measured on `dev` at `64ff609`, with real `Calendars` / `Events` stores and the mounted `Neo.calendar.view.month.Component`, counting `neo-week` rows:

| calendars | events | weeks after mount |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | **0** |
| 1 | 0, store loaded | 18 |
| 1 | store never loaded | **0** |
| 1 | 1 | 18 |

A month grid should show its days whatever the data. Two cases leave it blank: a calendar store with no records, and an event store whose load never happens, for example a failed request.

## The Architectural Reality

`src/calendar/view/month/Component.mjs` builds the grid in `createContent()`. Every path that reaches it on first render first asks for a store count:

- `construct()` sets `needsEventUpdate` only when both stores have records;
- `afterSetMounted()` calls `createContent()` only when `needsEventUpdate` is set;
- `onEventStoreLoad()` builds only when the calendar store has records, and `onCalendarStoreLoad()` only when the event store has records.

The constructor check comes from #2460, which fixed a race: a lazily loaded view can arrive after both stores have loaded. A count cannot tell "loaded and empty" from "not loaded yet", so the check that fixed the race also blocks the empty case.

## The Fix

The days render on mount whatever the stores hold. Events still need both stores.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With no calendars and no events, the mounted month view renders 18 `neo-week` rows and 126 `neo-day` cells.
- [ ] With one calendar and an event store that has not loaded, the days render.
- [ ] With calendars and events loaded, the events render in their day cells, as before.
- [ ] An event whose calendar is not in the calendar store does not throw.
- [ ] A component-tier spec covers the no-calendar mount (@sloemo01's `calendar-month` fixture fits).
- [ ] `npm run test-components` and `npm run test-unit` pass.

## Out of Scope

- The week and year views use the same count check (`week/Component.mjs` `construct()`, `YearComponent.mjs` `construct()`). Whether they also render empty has not been measured.
- #19006's other assertions.

## Avoided Traps

- **Dropping the count checks outright.** `createWeek()` reads `calendarStore.get(record.calendarId).active`. With zero calendars and one event, that throws a `TypeError` today (measured). The events need the calendars, so the days are what must stop waiting.
- **Re-breaking #2460.** The view can be constructed after both stores have loaded, so a load listener alone never fires.

## Related

#19006 (where this was found) · #2460 (the race the constructor check fixed) · #18985

### @sloemo01 - 2026-09-23T18:59:30Z

Taking the fix, and the fixture with it.

The three premises hold on today's `dev` at `18b473b6e8`, measured against a live server rather than reasoned from the source:

```
after mount      weeks 0   days 0   events 0
addCalendar      weeks 0   days 0
addEvent         weeks 18  days 126 events 1
```

The first two lines are the defect: the days wait for a store count. The third is the same component drawing correctly the moment a matched pair arrives, through `onEventStoreLoad`, which is what makes it a mount-path defect and not a grid that cannot draw.

One thing the ticket lists as an avoided trap that I have to disagree with, with a measurement. The ticket says `createWeek` reads `calendarStore.get(record.calendarId).active` and that zero calendars with one event throws a `TypeError` today. It does not, on this head: `Store#get` answers `undefined` for a missing key and the read through it is what would throw, but no path reaches that line with zero calendars because `createContent` was never called. Once the mount path is fixed the read becomes reachable, so I am guarding it in the same PR — the trap is real, it just is not reachable until this fix lands, and a spec arm covers it.

The fixture you offered is not on disk, or in any branch: `git log --all --diff-filter=A` over `test/playwright/component/apps/calendar-month/` returns nothing. I described it on #19006 and never committed it, so I am building it here instead of recovering it.

- 2026-09-24T12:41:46Z @tobiu referenced in commit `67bee04` - "fix(calendar): the month grid draws its days on mount, whatever the stores hold (#19149) (#19150)

* fix(calendar): the month grid draws its days on mount, whatever the stores hold (#19149)

`construct` set `needsEventUpdate` only when both stores reported a count above zero, and
`afterSetMounted` built the grid only behind that flag. A month with no calendars therefore never
reached `createContent`, so a view whose data had not arrived rendered its header and an empty
scroll area — `weekCount: 0, dayCount: 0` measured on a live server.

The days are the grid's frame and do not depend on data, so `construct` now builds them
unconditionally. Events keep needing their calendars: `createContent` calls `createWeek` per row,
and `createWeek` reads each event's calendar for its color class, so an event whose calendar is
absent is skipped rather than drawn. That read is reachable for the first time with this fix, so it
is guarded here — `Store#get` answers `undefined` for a missing key.

The #2460 race is untouched: that fix made a view constructed after both stores loaded build its
events, and it still does, through `onEventStoreLoad`.

The fixture and spec are new; the calendar-month fixture described on #19006 was never committed.
